To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Knowledge Vault is a large-scale, Web-scale probabilistic knowledge base; (2) Knowledge Vault combines information from multiple sources including text, tables, page structure, human annotations, and existing knowledge bases; and (3) The Knowledge Vault is calibrated and has a high level of precision.

The Knowledge Vault is a probabilistic knowledge base, constructed using a combination of extractions from Web sources and prior knowledge from existing knowledge repositories, that can be used for many applications, including information retrieval and question answering.

(i) the Knowledge Vault is the largest knowledge base to date; (ii) the Knowledge Vault has the most accurate probabilistic estimates; (iii) the Knowledge Vault can be used to answer complex questions about the world; and (iv) the Knowledge Vault will be useful to a wide range of users, such as search engine developers, knowledge base developers, and end users.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can we combine the information from diverse sources to build a large knowledge base that can be used for answering complex queries and for improving the performance of other applications? Can we automatically infer probabilistic correctness of facts, and how does it help in building a knowledge base? Can we use a probabilistic knowledge base to improve the accuracy of other tasks such as question answering and information retrieval?
